note: Generated by FPGA_Design_Agent_Knowledge tools/family_matrix.py --site-json (brief 31). Our own one-line summaries.

rows.summary: Zynq-7000 offers M/S_AXI_GP (32-bit), S_AXI_HP0-3 (64-bit) and S_AXI_ACP; Zynq UltraScale+ offers HPM0/1_FPD, HPM0_LPD, HPC0/1, HP0-3, ACP, ACE and S_AXI_LPD, up to 128 bits.

rows.topic: AXI protocol version at the PS boundary
rows.summary: The Zynq-7000 PS ports are AXI3 (16-beat bursts, write IDs); the Zynq UltraScale+ PS ports are AXI4, so interconnect conversion needs differ.
Zynq-7000 gives FCLK_CLK0-3 and FCLK_RESET0-3_N; Zynq UltraScale+ gives pl_clk0-3 and pl_resetn0-3, which software drives as PS GPIOs.
Zynq UltraScale+ has separate LPD, FPD and PL power domains with PS-PL isolation that must be released; Zynq-7000 has no such isolation.

rows.topic: Cache coherency of PL DMA buffers
rows.summary: Zynq-7000: one I/O-coherent port (ACP), 32-byte lines; Zynq UltraScale+: HPC0/1 coherent only when the master marks its transfers and CCI snooping is on, 64-byte lines, a line-only ACP.

The PL interrupt lines reach the GIC at different IDs: Zynq-7000 IRQ_F2P[7:0] are 61-68 and [15:8] are 84-91; Zynq UltraScale+ pl_ps_irq0 is 121-128 and pl_ps_irq1 136-143 (device-tree SPI number = ID - 32).

zynq7000_ps.use: GP/HP/ACP ports, AXI3, HP FIFOs and QoS

common.use: AXI reference (protocol rules shared by both)

rows.summary: 7-series carry runs 4 bits per slice (CARRY4); UltraScale+ runs 8 bits per CLB (CARRY8), so adder delay per bit and the packing of short adders differ.
A single DSP takes 25 x 18 on 7-series and 27 x 18 on UltraScale+, which changes how wide multipliers and fixed-point formats split across slices.
The same RTL adder or multiplier closes at different clocks: -1 Artix-7 is the slowest of the owner's targets and the K26 -2LV runs at VCCINT 0.72 V.
Per-operator delays used to choose pipeline depth and hard resources before any build are measured per family; a 7-series model must not be reused on UltraScale+.
report_synchronizer_mtbf works only on UltraScale and UltraScale+ parts; on 7-series MTBF must be estimated by hand from the stage count.
XPM_CDC macros, ASYNC_REG and report_cdc behave the same on both families; the difference is only in the primitives underneath.
Both Zynq families clock PS-PL AXI ports from a PL-supplied clock and cross inside the PS, but ZU+ adds the LPD/FPD split, so a crossing into a powered-down domain behaves differently.
MMCM VCO is 600-1200 MHz on a -1 7-series part but 800-1600 MHz on the K26; a ZU+ multiplier can be illegal on Artix-7.
7-series PLLE2 is a general clock generator; the UltraScale+ PLLE4 has no external feedback or deskew and is meant for I/O PHY clocking.
BUFR, BUFIO, BUFMR and BUFH exist only on 7-series; UltraScale+ uses BUFGCE, BUFGCE_DIV, BUFG_GT and BUFG_PS, and synthesis maps BUFG to BUFGCE.
A 7-series clock region spans half the device width; UltraScale+ regions are fixed-size tiles with segmented routing and distribution tracks, controlled with CLOCK_ROOT.
7-series has MRCC/SRCC clock-capable pins; UltraScale+ has GC pins on HP banks and HDGC pins on HD banks, and HDGC reaches only BUFGCE.
MMCME4 can change an output divider without a reset (CDDC); MMCME2 output changes need the DRP and a reset or relock.
Vivado retargets some 7-series clocking primitives on UltraScale+: an MMCME2_ADV in RTL synthesises to MMCME4_ADV, but the VCO limits then follow the new part.
CLOCK_DEDICATED_ROUTE values differ: 7-series takes TRUE, BACKBONE or FALSE; UltraScale+ adds SAME_CMT_COLUMN and ANY_CMT_COLUMN, which 7-series does not have.

rows.summary: 7-series designs need CFGBVS and CONFIG_VOLTAGE in the XDC (DRC CFGBVS-1 otherwise); on the K26 that check does not fire.
LVCMOS33 or LVCMOS25 constraints on a K26 HP pin fail DRC BIVB-1; the same lines are legal on Artix-7 HR and K26 HD pins.
CLOCK_DEDICATED_ROUTE values differ, and USER_CLOCK_ROOT and CLOCK_DELAY_GROUP exist only for UltraScale and later.

rows.topic: I/O delay constraints and delay primitives
rows.summary: set_input_delay and set_output_delay are written the same way, but the IDELAY that absorbs the window is 32 x 78 ps on 7-series and calibrated picoseconds on UltraScale+.
AUTOPIPELINE_* properties are for UltraScale, UltraScale+ and Versal only; 7-series has no auto-pipelining.

rows.topic: Clock uncertainty parts and MMCM jitter
rows.summary: The same uncertainty fields (system, input, discrete jitter, phase error, user) on every family; the MMCM's jitter and phase error, and so the numbers, are per family and speed grade.

rows.topic: Input capture hold at the IOB
rows.summary: On 7-series a BUFG-clocked IOB input flip-flop gets a fixed hold-compensating delay; BUFIO and MMCM captures do not, so their hold must be designed (IDELAY, feedback BUFG).
For a performance goal, UltraScale+ adds auto-pipelining, ML strategies and IDR; on 7-series the goal is met with directives, retiming and RTL pipelining only.
Area is counted in different units: Artix-7 slices hold 4 LUTs, UltraScale+ CLBs hold 8, and URAM and DSP48E2 width change which resource a memory or multiplier uses.
UltraRAM auto-sleep and BRAM sleep exist only on UltraScale+; power_opt_design clock gating is common; the K26 low-voltage grade changes the static baseline.
DSP48E1 multiplies 25 x 18 with a 25-bit pre-adder; DSP48E2 multiplies 27 x 18 with a 27-bit pre-adder, so a 27-bit coefficient fits one slice only on UltraScale+.

rows.topic: Wide XOR and fourth ALU operand
rows.summary: DSP48E2 adds a wide XOR (up to 96 bits per slice) and a W multiplexer for a fourth operand or rounding constant; DSP48E1 has neither.

rows.topic: DSP primitive is a macro on UltraScale+
rows.summary: DSP48E2 is a macro of several lib cells in Vivado, so netlist queries by REF_NAME or lib cell behave differently from DSP48E1.
FIR, DDS and multiplier IP use the family's DSP slice, so latency, slice count and the fastest clock differ between Artix-7 and the K26 for the same settings.

ultrascale_plus.use: DSP48E2 27 x 18, wide XOR, W mux, 'Differences from Previous Generations'

common.use: FIR Compiler resources and latency per family

rows.summary: fsm_encoding, fsm_safe_state and -fsm_extraction behave the same in Vivado synthesis for both families; no family rule applies.
SEM for 7-series is PG036 (FRAME_ECCE2, ICAPE2); SEM for UltraScale and UltraScale+ is PG187 (FRAME_ECCE3/E4, ICAPE3) with different modes and interfaces.
POST_CRC (continuous readback CRC) is a 7-series property; UltraScale+ uses its own configuration settings for the same check.

rows.topic: Reset styles and flop primitives for a state register
rows.summary: Async reset maps to FDCE/FDPE, sync to FDRE/FDSE, none to FDRE with an initial value, with the same LUT, flop and control-set counts on 7-series and UltraScale+ for the same RTL (synthesis only).

ultrascale_plus.use: UltraScale SEM incl. migration to UltraScale+

hil.name: Configuration, debug and hardware in the loop

rows.summary: STARTUPE2, ICAPE2 and FRAME_ECCE2 are 7-series; UltraScale+ has STARTUPE3 (with the SPI data pins and DONE), ICAPE3 (AVAIL, PRDONE) and FRAME_ECCE4.
The Nexys A7 PL is programmed straight over JTAG; on the ZedBoard and K26 the PL can be loaded over JTAG, but PS clocks, resets and isolation need the PS init script first.

rows.topic: Device DNA and user eFUSE access
rows.summary: DNA_PORT (57-bit DNA) is 7-series and DNA_PORTE2 is UltraScale+; the pins are the same but the shift length differs, so read the length from the family guide.
ILA, VIO and JTAG-to-AXI work the same way on all families; on Zynq parts the debug hub clock must come from a running PL clock, which on the PS boards means after PS init.
The USR_ACCESS bitstream setting and the USR_ACCESSE2 primitive exist on 7 series, UltraScale+ and both Zynq PLs (UG908 tables); measured on 7 series only.

7series.use: USR_ACCESS build identification, AXSS write in the bitstream

rows.summary: Artix-7 and the Zynq-7020 have only HR banks (1.2-3.3 V); the K26 has HP banks (1.8 V maximum) and HD banks (up to 3.3 V).
IDELAYE2 has 32 taps of about 78 ps at a 200 MHz reference; IDELAYE3 has 512 taps of 2.1-12 ps and a TIME mode that holds a delay in picoseconds across voltage and temperature.
ISERDESE2/OSERDESE2 take widths up to 8 (14 cascaded) with BITSLIP; UltraScale+ ISERDESE3/OSERDESE3 take 4 or 8 with no bitslip, and native mode (RX/TX_BITSLICE) is a different design style.
On HR banks LVDS_25 outputs need VCCO 2.5 V and DIFF_TERM; on UltraScale+ HP banks LVDS runs at 1.8 V with DIFF_TERM_ADV, plus ODT and PRE_EMPHASIS that 7-series lacks.
Artix-7 has GTP transceivers (none on the Nexys A7 part) and the Zynq-7020 has none; the K26 has GTH transceivers with different wizards and reference-clock buffers.
7-series slices have CARRY4 and MUXF7/F8; UltraScale+ CLBs have one CARRY8 and MUXF9, and a 7-series CARRY4 instance has no ZU+ lib cell.

Artix-7 and the ZU+ PL have no hard Ethernet MAC: a fabric MAC drives a PHY through SelectIO (RMII, MII, RGMII). Both Zynq PS families have hard GEMs: RGMII through MIO, GMII through EMIO to PL logic.
RGMII's DDR registers are IDDR/ODDR on 7-series and IDDRE1/ODDRE1 on UltraScale+; both have a same-edge-pipelined input mode, but ODDRE1 has no opposite-edge mode.

rows.topic: LUT RAM shapes for table emulation
rows.summary: Both families have 32-, 64-, 128- and 256-deep single-bit LUT RAMs; UltraScale+ adds RAM32M16, RAM64M8, RAM256X1D and RAM512X1S, so wide multi-port shapes and 512-deep columns exist only there.

rows.topic: Wizard and IP names per family
rows.summary: Several wizards are family-specific: XADC Wizard against System Management Wizard, MIG 7 Series against the DDR4 SDRAM IP, SelectIO Wizard against High Speed SelectIO Wizard, PS7 against PS8.
The Clocking Wizard is one IP but instantiates MMCME2/PLLE2 on 7-series and MMCME4/PLLE4 on UltraScale+, with the family's VCO limits and buffer types.

rows.topic: Built-in FIFO choice in FIFO Generator
rows.summary: FIFO Generator's built-in FIFO option maps to FIFO36E1 or FIFO36E2, whose resets and flag latencies differ; the common-clock and independent-clock BRAM options behave the same.
Generated IP (.xci) records its part; retargeting a project from the Nexys A7 to the K26 needs upgrade_ip and regeneration, and some IP has no equivalent.
UltraRAM (288 Kb, 4K x 72, one clock) exists on the K26 (64 blocks) but on no 7-series part; ram_style ultra has nothing to map to on Artix-7.
RAMB36E2 cascades data in the BRAM column (CASCADE_ORDER) with no fabric logic; RAMB36E1 only pairs two halves for a 64K x 1 memory.
Both families have 64-bit ECC in a RAMB36 in SDP mode; only RAMB36E2 adds an ECC pipeline register (EN_ECC_PIPE) for higher clock rates.
FIFO36E2 is not backward compatible with FIFO36E1: reset becomes synchronous, flag latencies change and asymmetric widths appear.
PL DRAM on Artix-7 uses MIG for DDR2/DDR3 on HR banks; the K26 uses the PS DDR4 controller, and a PL DDR4 controller (PG150) needs HP banks.
Both PS families have 256 KB OCM, but its address map and PL access path differ (Zynq-7000 through the GP/ACP ports, ZU+ through HPM/HPC/ACP and the LPD).

rows.summary: 7-series has the XADC (two 12-bit 1 MSPS ADCs, external analog inputs); UltraScale+ has SYSMONE4 (10-bit, 200 kSPS), which adds I2C/PMBus and user supply monitors.
Both blocks raise over-temperature alarms, but on ZU+ the PS and PL monitors are separate and the PMU firmware also acts on them.

rows.summary: 7-series -1 parts run VCCINT at 1.0 V; the K26 -2LV runs VCCINT at 0.72 V, which report_power and the timing models must both assume.
On Zynq parts report_power includes the PS from the PS block settings; on Artix-7 there is none, so on-chip totals are not comparable across boards.
Vectorless defaults (12.5% toggle, 0.5 static probability) are the same for every family; what differs is the device static power and the thermal model.
Generic RTL and XPM macros port between families; instantiated 7-series primitives (BUFR, IDELAYE2, XADC, CARRY4, STARTUPE2) have no UltraScale+ lib cell and must be rewritten.
AMD advises removing 7-series LOC, RLOC and mapping constraints before implementing on UltraScale; site names and slice structure differ.
A Zynq-7000 block design (processing_system7) cannot be retargeted to Zynq UltraScale+; the PS block, port names and board presets are rebuilt.

ultrascale_plus.use: porting advice: remove mapping and placement constraints

rows.summary: UltraScale+ CLBs have four clock enables per CLB and an optional set/reset inversion, so control-set pressure that hurts Artix-7 packing is milder on the K26.

rows.topic: Synchronous resets for UltraRAM and DSP
rows.summary: On UltraScale+ an asynchronously reset flop driving UltraRAM control pins can corrupt contents, so the synchronous-reset rule is stronger than on 7-series.
UltraScale+ has MUXF9 (a 64:1 mux within one CLB); 7-series stops at MUXF8 (16:1 per slice).
The same Vivado inference templates work on both families; what changes is the target (URAM only on ZU+, DSP48E2 pre-adder width, SRL and LUTRAM are the same).

rows.topic: VHDL-2008 acceptance and VHDL warnings in synthesis
rows.summary: No family difference found: 22 VHDL probes (2008 features, drivers, latches, resets, INIT, FSM, mixed language, port case) gave the same results on xc7a100t, xc7z020 and xck26 in Vivado 2026.1.

ultrascale_plus.use: CLB control sets, MUXF9, latch option

rows.topic: ML strategies and Intelligent Design Runs
rows.summary: ML strategies, Intelligent Design Runs and the ML part of report_qor_assessment are supported only for UltraScale and UltraScale+, not 7-series.

rows.topic: Versal Advanced Flow notes in the 2026.1 guides
rows.summary: UG904's Advanced Flow (and its list of features not supported in it) applies to Versal only; it does not change 7-series or UltraScale+ flows.
Auto-pipelining and SLR-crossing optimisation in phys_opt_design need UltraScale or later; the rest of phys_opt_design is common.
Incremental implementation works on both families; the reference checkpoint must come from the same part, so it never carries across families.
report_design_analysis congestion levels are defined per architecture; 7-series and UltraScale tables differ, so thresholds do not carry over.
On UltraScale+ synthesis retargets some 7-series primitives (BUFG to BUFGCE, MMCME2_ADV to MMCME4_ADV) but not regional buffers, IDELAYE2, XADC or CARRY4, which have no lib cell.

common.use: IDR and ML strategy support, congestion tables per family

rows.summary: UNISIM models are per family: a testbench that instantiates IDELAYE2, XADC or MMCME2 needs the 7-series models, and the UltraScale+ models add SIM_DEVICE and calibration behaviour.
Zynq-7000 and Zynq UltraScale+ have different PS VIPs (processing_system7_vip against zynq_ultra_ps_e_vip) with different port names and APIs.
Formal checks and lint of plain RTL do not depend on family; only black-boxed primitives differ, so the stub set must match the target family.
Only Zynq UltraScale+ has an AMD-published safety integrity statement per power domain; the 7-series and Zynq-7000 overviews carry only the safety disclaimer.
TMDS_33 is an HR-bank standard: it works on Artix-7 and Zynq-7020 HR banks, but UltraScale+ has no HR banks, so the K26 needs another route to HDMI.
UltraScale+ HP banks have a native MIPI D-PHY receiver (MIPI_DPHY_DCI); 7-series needs an external resistor network and LVDS inputs.
The K26 (an EV device) has a hardened video codec unit and a PS GPU; 7-series and Zynq-7000 have no video hard blocks.
